name: Veneers / Turkey teeth

card.summary: Thin ceramic or composite shells bonded over teeth for a uniform smile; durable in studies, but preparation can remove enamel and the cheap multi-tooth 'Turkey teeth' packages draw scrutiny.
card.aka: Hollywood smile, Turkey teeth, laminate veneers
card.note: Prepared teeth cannot regrow enamel; outcomes depend on how much tooth is removed and on bonding technique.

quick.overview:
Veneers are thin shells of porcelain or composite resin bonded to the front of teeth to change colour, shape or apparent alignment. Wikipedia notes they are sometimes nicknamed 'Turkey teeth' in reference to dental tourism, and 'Hollywood smile' is the name for multi-tooth makeovers.

Systematic reviews of ceramic laminate veneers report high survival rates over about a decade. In looksmaxxing forums, veneers are discussed as a way to improve the smile and sometimes as a stand-in for orthodontics, including on trips to Turkey.
quick.mechanism: The dentist usually removes a thin layer of enamel (the amount varies, and some systems use little or none), takes an impression or digital scan, and bonds a veneer made in a lab or chairside. Reviews stress that bonding to enamel, rather than exposed dentin, and proper surface treatment of the ceramic are linked to better outcomes.
quick.risks: Reported complications include chipping, debonding, marginal staining, sensitivity and decay. Preparation that exposes dentin is associated with lower success rates, and the loss of enamel is not reversible. Critics cited by Wikipedia describe overuse of veneers on healthy teeth as 'instant orthodontics'.

lead: A dental veneer is a layer of material, most often dental porcelain or composite resin, bonded to the front surface of a tooth to change its colour, shape, size or apparent position. [1] Laminate veneers are mostly cosmetic and cover only the facial surface, while full veneer crowns cover all coronal surfaces. [1] Multi-tooth cosmetic makeovers are commonly called 'Hollywood smile' treatments, and the term 'Turkey teeth' has become a nickname for veneers or crowns obtained cheaply at dental clinics in Turkey. [1]

The clinical literature on ceramic laminate veneers is substantial. A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies reported pooled survival of about 96% for feldspathic, 94% for leucite-reinforced and 97% for lithium disilicate veneers at around 10 years, with technical complications more frequent for feldspathic ceramics. [2] A 2024 narrative review similarly found satisfactory survival and success for these ceramics, with dentin exposure lowering success. [3]

In looksmaxxing communities veneers are described as a high-impact change to facial appearance, and posters discuss dental work as part of surgery trips to Turkey. [4][5] The research literature covers the clinical performance of veneers; no studies were identified on the 'Turkey teeth' practice as a defined phenomenon.
infobox: Feldspathic, lithium disilicate or other ceramics; composite resin
About 10 years survival in reviews; Wikipedia cites 10-30 years for modern veneers

paras: Composite veneers can be built directly on the tooth, or made outside the mouth and bonded; porcelain veneers are made indirectly. [1][6] Wikipedia says composite lasts about four years and porcelain is more durable and stains less, although other sources report longer composite survival. [1] A review of the direct-indirect composite technique describes advantages such as try-in before luting and improved marginal adaptation. [6]

A review of anterior veneer restorations argued that the evidence supporting some newer materials does not justify their use over established techniques, and that direct composite veneers remain widely used and are usually more affordable than indirect ones. [7] Digital design and CAD/CAM manufacture are increasingly used. [8][9]

Wikipedia credits California dentist Charles Pincus with inventing veneers in 1928 for a film shoot and with making acrylic veneers held by denture adhesive in 1937. [1] Michael Buonocore's work on acid etching in 1959 and the 1982 demonstration that porcelain could be etched with hydrofluoric acid led to veneers bonded to enamel. [1] A 2018 update on porcelain veneers provides historical background and discusses preparation designs, and a 2000 literature review examined the parameters for long-term success. [10][11]

A 2025 meta-analysis (29 studies, minimum one-year follow-up) found no difference in survival between feldspathic, leucite-reinforced and lithium disilicate veneers, with complication rates at about 10 years of roughly 41%, 30% and 6% for technical events respectively; zirconia veneers showed full survival but only 2.6 years of data. [2] A 2024 review reported that none of 55 studies met criteria for zirconia laminate veneers. [3]

A randomized split-mouth trial followed indirect resin composite and ceramic laminate veneers for up to 10 years, and a randomized trial compared CAD/CAM lithium disilicate veneers with heat-pressed ones. [12][13] Systematic review of anterior composite restorations has examined long-term survival and reasons for failure. [14] Registered trials include studies of prefabricated versus 3D-printed composite veneers, zirconia laminate veneers, and cementation techniques. [15][16][17]
Laboratory work includes measurement of tooth structure removed by different preparation designs, where veneer preparations were found less invasive than complete-coverage crown preparations. [18]

Wikipedia lists contraindications including poor oral hygiene, gum disease and unrealistic expectations, and notes that preparation can cause sensitivity and decay and that veneers can fail or need replacement. [1] Reviews report that bonding to dentin gives poorer results than bonding to enamel, and that immediate dentin sealing is used to improve bonding in indirect restorations. [3][19]
Preparation designs vary from conservative to extensive, and the 2002 study of tooth structure removal reported large differences between designs. [18]

On looksmax.org, users discuss veneers as improving apparent health and facial harmony; one thread's replies say veneers make a face look healthier. [20] Another poster asks about having veneers or crowns made in Turkey to address an underbite. [5] A forum post announcing a Turkey trip lists veneers among about a dozen procedures with a stated cost of about $15,000. [4]

timeline.event: Charles Pincus invents veneers for a film shoot (per Wikipedia). [1]
Michael Buonocore's enamel-etching work paves the way for bonded veneers. [1]
Simonsen and Calamia show porcelain can be etched with hydrofluoric acid. [1]
Update on porcelain veneers reviews materials and long-term studies up to 12 years. [10]
Meta-analysis of 29 studies reports high 10-year ceramic veneer survival. [2]

lore.intro: Veneers come up on looksmax.org as a smile upgrade and as one part of multi-procedure trips to Turkey. [4][20]

claims.claim: Veneers make a face look healthier and more attractive.
claims.believers: Replies in one thread say veneers make someone look 'way more NT and healthy'. [20]
claims.experts: Dental reviews study survival, complications and esthetic events of veneers rather than perceived attractiveness; no study in the sources assesses facial attractiveness. [2][3]

claims.claim: Veneers or crowns can fix an underbite.
claims.believers: One user asks whether Turkish dentists can use veneers or crowns for an underbite. [5]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes critics describe veneers on healthy teeth as 'instant orthodontics', and reviews cover veneers as restorations of tooth appearance rather than skeletal correction. [1][7]

claims.claim: Dental work in Turkey is a cost-effective way to get veneers.
claims.believers: A poster flying to Antalya for a long list of procedures describes the budget as about $15,000 and takes questions from the thread. [4]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports veneers are widely offered in Istanbul, Ankara and Antalya, and general medical-tourism reviews describe variable follow-up care; no outcome studies of Turkish veneer packages were identified. [21][1]

claims.claim: Preparing teeth for veneers permanently removes enamel.
claims.believers: No forum source in the reviewed material specifically addresses enamel loss; discussion centres on appearance outcomes. [20]
claims.experts: Studies quantify tooth reduction by preparation design, and reviews state that dentin exposure lowers veneer success. [18][3]
